title: Design and Construction of an Ultra-Low Carbon House in the UK—A Case Study
content: The study evaluates the potential to reduce both embodied and operational carbon in a 10UK domestic case study building through a combination of reduced concrete use, bio- 11based building materials, on-site photovoltaic generation, and high-performance building 12services. The embodied A1-A4 fossil carbon has been calculated to be 321.00kg CO2e/m2, 13which could be readily reduced to 286.85kg CO2e/m2 by making substitutions for 4 ele- 14ments within the building (underfloor insulation, roof covering, kitchen worktops and 15floor coverings) which is below the LETI 2030 target of 300kg CO2e/m2 and, accounting 16for biogenic carbon, to be better than zero overall embodied carbon. Operational energy 17is net negative, with consumption being only 35% of the energy generated by PV, and the 18overall annual financial cost was a negative £393.75 refunded by the supplier. 19Consideration is given to the treatment of bio-based construction materials in the evalua- tion of the whole life carbon impact of a building and proposes that the environmental benefits of construction materials made from short cycle crops should be better accounted for.
